front_matter.purpose:
# Purpose

This Policy & Procedure Manual sets out how **[AGENCY NAME]** (the "Agency"), a Licensed Home Care Services Agency (LHCSA) licensed by the New York State Department of Health (DOH) with Public Health and Health Planning Council (PHHPC) approval under Public Health Law Article 36 and 10 NYCRR Parts 765–766, delivers, supervises, documents and manages home care services. It also covers Medicaid personal care services under 18 NYCRR §505.14, paid mainly through Managed Long Term Care (MLTC) plans.

The Manual is intended to:

- Turn the regulatory requirements that govern the Agency into written, day-to-day procedures that staff can follow.
- Protect patient rights, safety and confidentiality, and support continuity and quality of care.
- Define the responsibilities of the governing authority, the RN who directs and supervises patient care, supervisory staff, aides and contracted personnel.
- Give the Agency a consistent basis for DOH review, the pre-opening survey, surveillance, and plan and payer audits.

**Customization, adoption and maintenance.** This Manual is a template. It is not effective until the Agency has done the following:

1. **Customize it.** Replace every [AGENCY NAME] placeholder and every other bracketed field (counties and services authorized, office and branch locations, names and titles, committee membership, contracted plans and vendors). Edit each policy so it matches what the Agency actually does and its license, approved services and payer contracts. Delete any section that does not apply, such as advanced home health aide (AHHA) provisions if the Agency does not use AHHAs.
2. **Have the governing authority adopt it.** Under 10 NYCRR §766.9(d), the governing authority adopts and amends the Agency's policies. Record adoption, and each later amendment, in the governing authority's minutes with the date.
3. **Keep it current.** 10 NYCRR §766.2(a)(1) requires policies to be reviewed and revised as necessary, and 10 NYCRR §766.11(a) requires personnel policies to be reviewed at least annually. The QI committee also reviews policies under 10 NYCRR §766.9(l). Regulations, DOH guidance and payer contracts change, so verify each citation against the current text before relying on it.
4. **Train staff on it.** All care staff must know patient rights (10 NYCRR §766.1(b)), and orientation and in-service training are required (10 NYCRR §766.11(i)). Orient all employees to the emergency plan (10 NYCRR §766.9(c)). Document each person's training on this Manual, and retrain whenever a policy materially changes.

This Manual is not legal advice. It does not replace the regulations, DOH directives or the Agency's contracts. If this Manual conflicts with a law, regulation or contract, the law, regulation or contract controls. The Agency should have the Manual reviewed by qualified counsel or a consultant before adoption.

# How to Use This Manual

**Who should use it.** The governing authority, administrator, RN supervisor or director of patient services, QI committee, intake and scheduling staff, human resources, billing staff, and all nurses, home health aides and personal care aides.

**Getting started**

1. Read the Regulatory Framework section to see which rules apply and where each comes from.
2. Find and replace every **[AGENCY NAME]** placeholder and every bracketed field. Search the finished document for remaining brackets before adoption.
3. Confirm the points flagged below as needing verification, and update the affected policies.
4. Route the draft to the governing authority for adoption, and record the adoption date and version number.
5. Issue the Manual to staff, deliver and document training, and keep signed acknowledgments in personnel records.

**Using it day to day**

- Use the table of contents to find the policy that matches the task, such as intake, plan of care, supervision, records, personnel, complaints or discharge. Each policy should point to the regulation it implements.
- Follow the procedures as written. If a procedure does not match actual practice, change the practice or have the governing authority change the policy. Do not leave the gap in place.
- Keep forms, logs and registers named in the procedures where they can be produced for DOH on request.
- When a regulator, plan or contract changes a requirement, tell the administrator and the RN supervisor. They should start a revision and bring it to the governing authority.

**Review and revision cycle**

- Review all patient service policies as often as needed, and document the review (10 NYCRR §766.2(a)(1)).
- Review personnel policies at least annually (10 NYCRR §766.11(a)).
- Review policies at the QI committee, which meets at least four times a year, and send its written summary to the governing authority (10 NYCRR §766.9(l)).
- Keep a revision log showing the date, the sections changed, the reason and the governing authority's approval. Keep superseded versions according to the retention periods in 10 NYCRR §766.12.

**Types of authority cited.** The Manual separates binding law from guidance:

- **Statutes and regulations** (Public Health Law and NYCRR) set binding requirements.
- **DOH policy documents, Dear Administrator Letters (DALs), review tools and OMIG audit guidance** show how regulators interpret and check compliance. They may not create independent legal requirements. In particular, the DOH P&P Review Tool is a useful surveyor's checklist, and the OMIG personal care audit protocol is audit guidance only.
- **Payer contracts**, such as MLTC plan agreements, add requirements that this template cannot state. Insert the contract terms (for example, the required frequency of RN supervisory visits) in the appropriate policies.

**Items to verify before adoption.** Some source texts were only partly reviewed when this template was prepared. Confirm the full, current text of the following and revise the related policies if needed:

- 10 NYCRR §766.10 (contracts), including subdivision (f) on personal care contracts with local social services districts.
- 10 NYCRR §700.2 (aide qualifications and training definitions).
- 18 NYCRR §505.14(e) (personal care aide training) and §505.14(f) (nursing supervision frequency). DOH rulemaking has reportedly shifted the supervision-frequency determination to the local district or MMCO, so state the required frequency on each plan of care or in the contract.
- Current rates, wage and wage-parity amounts, and reporting windows, which change over time.

# Regulatory Framework

The Agency operates under the laws and regulations below. They are listed by their exact citations. The list is not exhaustive. The governing authority is responsible for compliance with all applicable laws (10 NYCRR §766.9(a)-(b)).

## 1. Licensure and Agency Operations

| Citation | Subject |
|---|---|
| Public Health Law §3605 | Licensure of home care services agencies. A license is required to provide nursing, home health aide or personal care services. PHHPC approval considers public need, character and competence, and financial resources. |
| Public Health Law §3605-b | Annual LHCSA registration. Unregistered agencies may not operate or be paid. Late registration carries a penalty, and missing two registration periods can lead to revocation. |
| 10 NYCRR §765-1.2; §765-1.16 | Application review standards (character, competence, financial feasibility) and determinations of public need. |
| 10 NYCRR §700.2 | Definitions, including home care services agency and licensed home care services agency, and aide qualifications. *Confirm the full text of the aide definitions.* |
| Public Health Law §3612 | Cost reporting, filed when DOH requires it. |
| 10 NYCRR §766.9 | Governing authority: responsibility for compliance, written emergency plan, policy adoption, public disclosure of services and charges, staffing, an RN to direct and supervise care, admission criteria, complaint procedure, QI program and committee, management contracts, franchise agreements, and Health Provider Network (HPN) requirements. |
| 10 NYCRR §766.10 | Contracts for patient care services. *Confirm the full text.* |
| 10 NYCRR §766.12 | Records and reports, required documents at the principal and branch offices, retention minimums, electronic records, and annual statistical and ownership submissions to DOH. |

## 2. Patient Rights, Care and Records

| Citation | Subject |
|---|---|
| 10 NYCRR §766.1 | Patient rights: written notice before care begins, statement of services and charges, payer and patient responsibility, participation in care planning, right to refuse care, complaints without reprisal, privacy, and representatives. |
| 10 NYCRR §766.2 | Patient service policies and procedures, continuity of personnel, caregiver ID, infection control for supplies and equipment, QI committee review of new nursing or therapeutic services, and discharge planning and notice. |
| 10 NYCRR §766.3 | Acceptance of patients, professional assessment, plan of care, and review at least every six months. |
| 10 NYCRR §766.5 | Clinical supervision, including RN supervision of aides and in-home supervisory visits. Paragraph (e) applies only if the Agency uses AHHAs. |
| 10 NYCRR §766.6 | Patient care record: contents, confidentiality, retention (at least 6 years after discharge, with longer periods for minors), and record safeguards. |

## 3. Personnel, Background Checks and the Home Care Worker Registry

| Citation | Subject |
|---|---|
| 10 NYCRR §766.11 | Personnel: annual policy review, aide qualifications, health status and immunizations, identity and reference verification, criminal history checks, orientation and in-service hours, job descriptions, annual performance assessment, and bloodborne pathogen program. |
| 10 NYCRR §402.6 | Criminal history record check process. |
| 10 NYCRR Part 403 (§403.3, §403.5(a)(6)) | Home Care Worker Registry: at least two designated registry users, implementing policies, and timely entry of employment information. |
| Public Health Law §3613 | Home Care Services Worker Registry and the information entered for each worker. |

## 4. Medicaid Personal Care and Managed Care

| Citation | Subject |
|---|---|
| 18 NYCRR §505.14(a)-(b) | Medicaid personal care services: scope, Level I and Level II tasks, minimum needs, continuous and live-in services, assessment and authorization. |
| 18 NYCRR §505.14(e) | Personal care aide training and qualifications. *Confirm the current text.* |
| 18 NYCRR §505.14(f) | Nursing supervision of personal care aides. *Confirm the current text and the MLTC contract.* |
| DOH Minimum Needs Requirements (PCS/CDPAS/MLTC) | Minimum needs requirements effective 9/1/2025. |
| DOH MLTC Policy: LHCSA contract limits | Limits on the number of LHCSAs an MLTC plan may contract with, and the exceptions process. |
| DOH Medicaid Managed Care NYIA guidance | The plan's responsibility for authorizations and for recording level, amount, frequency and duration in the plan of care. |
| DOH Electronic Visit Verification (21st Century Cures Act, 42 USC 1396b(l)) | EVV for Medicaid personal care services. |

## 5. Wages

| Citation | Subject |
|---|---|
| Public Health Law §3614-c | Home care worker wage parity in NYC, Nassau, Suffolk and Westchester, including annual certification, audited statements and record retention. |
| Public Health Law §3614-f | Home care aide minimum wage. |

## 6. Regulatory Guidance and Audit Tools (not independent legal requirements)

- **DOH DAL DHCBS 25-09:** weekly HERDS reporting by LHCSAs.
- **DOH DAL DHCBS 20-05 (1/30/2020):** verification of PCA/HHA/AHHA training documentation at hire.
- **NYSDOH LHCSA Policy & Procedure Manual Review Tool (Part B):** the checklist DOH reviewers use for P&P manuals.
- **DOH LHCSA Application Requirements FAQ (eff. 4/1/2020):** the P&P manual goes to the regional home care office after PHHPC contingent approval and must be accepted before the pre-opening survey.
- **OMIG Audit Protocol: Personal Care Aides (guidance, rev. 5/11/15):** audit criteria, including documentation of RN supervisory visits. This is audit guidance only.

## 7. Regulators and Contacts

The source material did not include telephone numbers. Confirm current phone numbers and mailing addresses on each regulator's website before inserting them in this Manual.

citations.title: Patient rights
citations.requirement: The governing authority must adopt written patient-rights policies and procedures. Patients get their rights in writing before care starts, with documentation in the clinical record (a)(1). They get a statement of services and charges (a)(2). They are told before care how much third-party payers are expected to pay and how much the patient must pay (a)(3). Any change must be given within 30 calendar days of the agency learning of it, orally and in writing (a)(3)(i)-(ii). Other rights: be told what services will be provided and by whom (a)(4); take part in care planning (a)(5); refuse care (a)(6); complain free of reprisal (a)(7)-(9); be treated with respect (a)(10); privacy of records (a)(11); refuse advanced home health aide tasks (a)(12). Agencies must tell patients they may complain to the DOH Office of Health Systems Management (a)(9). All care staff must know these rights (b). A legally authorized representative exercises the rights if the patient lacks capacity (c).

citations.title: Patient service policies and procedures
citations.requirement: Each service needs written policies and procedures, reviewed and revised as necessary (a)(1). Service delivery is documented in the clinical record (a)(2). Continuity: the same personnel serve the same patient where possible (a)(3). Caregivers carry current ID showing name, title, photo and agency name, returned on separation (a)(4). Written procedures cover storage, cleaning and disinfection of supplies and equipment (a)(5). Any new nursing or therapeutic service must go to the QI committee first (a)(7). A discharge plan starts before discharge (a)(8). Discharge happens only after notice to the authorized practitioner and consultation with the patient and staff, at least 48 hours before discharge (a)(9). "Health care services" are defined in (b) and include personal care.

citations.title: Plan of care
citations.requirement: A patient is accepted only after an RN, or a person directly supervised by an RN, determines the agency can safely and adequately meet the patient's needs (a). A plan of care is built on a professional assessment (b). It covers diagnosis, prognosis, mental status, frequency of each service, medications, treatments, diet, functional limitations and rehabilitation potential. The plan is reviewed and revised as often as needed, and at least every six months, with each review documented in the clinical record (d)(1). Staff promptly alert the authorized practitioner and other affected providers to significant changes in condition (d)(2).

citations.title: Clinical supervision
citations.requirement: The governing authority must ensure sufficient trained supervisory staff (a). Supervision includes case review, in-home visits to direct and evaluate care, clinical consultation, and consultation on policy. Evidence of adequate supervision (b): services delivered at the planned times and frequencies; assignment by licensure, training and demonstrated skill; prompt charting and reporting of changes in condition, adverse reactions, and problems with informal supports or the home; plans revised as needed. Aides are supervised "as appropriate" by an RN (c). In-home professional supervision occurs (d): (1) at the initial service visit or on a change in personnel, if the aide lacks documented training and experience in the tasks, with return demonstration; (2) when a change in condition occurs, to evaluate and revise the plan; (3) to instruct the aide on required observations and written reports. Paragraph (e) covers advanced home health aides (RN home visit at least every two weeks). Not applicable unless the agency uses AHHAs.

citations.title: Patient care record
citations.requirement: Each patient has a confidential record (a) containing: identifying data; medical orders; nursing assessments; the plan of care; signed and dated progress notes after each visit or phone contact; RN supervisory reports; aide observations and activity sheets; documentation of accidents and incidents (a)(8); documentation that rights information was received (a)(9); and a discharge summary (a)(10). Records are kept securely at least 6 years after discharge and are available to DOH (b). For minors, keep until 6 years after discharge or 3 years after age 18, whichever is longer (c). If the agency closes, the governing authority must arrange storage and access and notify DOH in writing where records are kept (d). Written policies must safeguard records against loss or unauthorized access and govern use, removal and release (e).

citations.title: Governing authority
citations.requirement: The governing authority is responsible for operation and compliance with all laws (a)-(b). It must keep a current written emergency plan and orient all employees to it (c). It adopts and amends policies (d) and makes public its services, service area, charges and payment mechanisms (e). It provides an adequate office with access to patient records and prompt phone contact (f). It employs enough staff (g). It employs at least one licensed, registered RN to direct and supervise all patient care (h). It accepts only patients whose needs can be met under written criteria (i). The complaint procedure (j) requires a complaint log; a written response within 15 days; notice of the right to appeal; appeal review by a governing-authority member or committee within 30 days; and notice of the right to complain to DOH. A continuous QI program is required (k). A QI committee with a consumer and health professionals meets at least four times a year (l): it reviews policies; reviews a random sample of current patients' and past-3-month discharges' records plus all complaint cases; and sends a written summary to the governing authority. Management contracts (m) and franchise agreements (n) need prior written commissioner consent; submit proposals at least 60 days before the effective date. Subdivision (o): HPN accounts, 24/7 emergency contacts, a written HPN coverage policy reviewed at least annually, and directory updates at least monthly.

citations.title: Contracts
citations.requirement: The agency may contract for patient care services. Services by arrangement require a written contract (b). Contract personnel must meet §766.11 personnel requirements (c). The agency remains responsible for the adequacy of contracted services (d). Nurses or therapists under contract must coordinate and integrate with agency services (e). Subdivision (f) addresses personal care contracts with local social services districts. Only the opening text of this section was seen; confirm the full text.

citations.title: Personnel
citations.requirement: Written personnel policies are reviewed at least annually (a). Aide qualifications under §700.2 must be met, and the PHL §3613(3)(a)-(f) information must be in the Home Care Registry (b). Health status is assessed before assuming duties (c). For personnel with direct patient contact (d): rubella immunity; measles immunity if born on or after 1/1/1957; TB risk assessment, symptom evaluation and TB test before employment and annually; an annual health status assessment; and influenza vaccination documentation or a mask during flu season. Identity is verified before hire (e). Employment history and references are verified before patient contact, and a criminal history record check is run as required by Part 402 (f). Personnel records hold verifications, licenses, evaluations and employment dates; health records are kept separate and confidential (g). Time and payment records are kept (h). Orientation is required, and in-service is at least 12 hours a year for HHAs, 6 for PCAs and 18 for AHHAs (i). Each position has a written job description (j). An annual performance assessment includes at least one in-home observation visit where applicable (k). A bloodborne-pathogen program (l) covers barriers, training at hire and yearly, PPE, monitoring, and an exposure-management procedure.

citations.title: Records and reports
citations.requirement: The agency must promptly submit all records and reports DOH requires (a). The principal NYS office keeps: the license, organizational documents, assumed-name certificate, patient-care contracts, governing-authority and QA bylaws, current policies, a current patient roster and a listing of all personnel (a)(1). Branch offices keep policies, a personnel list and patient records (a)(2). Retention minimums (a)(3): governing authority and committee minutes, 3 years; patient-care financial records, 3 years; personnel records, 3 years after separation; complaint and grievance records, 3 years after resolution; patient care records per §766.6. Electronic records must be secure, confidential and printable on request (b). Each year the agency furnishes DOH with statistical summaries of services and reimbursement, plus an ownership list (c).

citations.title: Definitions (home care services agency; licensed home care services agency; aide qualifications)
citations.requirement: Defines a home care services agency (a)(6) and a licensed home care services agency (a)(25) as one licensed under PHL Article 36. Per the fact-checked research, it also defines personal care aide and home health aide qualifications and training. The aide-definition text was past the truncation point in the fetch.

citations.title: Medicaid personal care services: scope, levels, minimum needs, assessment and authorization
citations.requirement: Personal care must be medically necessary, ordered by a qualified independent practitioner, based on assessment, delivered under a plan of care and supervised by an RN (a)(1). Eligibility requires a stable medical condition and self-direction, with the exceptions stated (a)(3)(i)-(ii). Minimum needs (a)(3)(iv): dementia or Alzheimer's needs supervision with more than one ADL; all others need limited assistance with physical maneuvering with more than two ADLs. Continuous PCS is more than 16 hours/day by more than one aide (a)(2). Live-in 24-hour PCS is one aide whose sleep is likely to be uninterrupted for 5 hours (a)(4). Level I covers nutritional and environmental support tasks only, authorized for no more than 8 hours/week (a)(5)(i). Level II adds personal care functions (a)(5)(ii)(a)(1)-(13), including medication prompting and assistance, but not administration (a)(5)(ii)(a)(10). Additional documentation is needed before authorizing more than 12 hours/day on average (a)(5)(ii)(b). Assessment (b): an independent RN assessment (RN licensed in NYS with 2+ years of home care experience), an independent medical exam and practitioner order, and plan development by the district or MMCO. Telehealth is allowed if an in-person option is offered.

citations.title: Personal care aide training and qualifications
citations.requirement: Per the fact-checked research: a personal care aide for Medicaid needs a DOH-approved HHA program or the 40-hour PCA basic training, completed within 3 months of hire, plus 3 hours of in-service semiannually. Subdivision (e) text was not seen in the truncated fetch.

citations.title: Nursing supervision of personal care aides
citations.requirement: Per the fact-checked research: an RN supervisory visit at least every 90 days, with a combined visit possible every six months for stable, self-directing clients. Later DOH rulemaking amended (f)(3)(vi) so the local district or MMCO determines the supervision frequency (regs.health.ny.gov summary of express terms). OMIG audit guidance says some counties require only six-month visits, so the frequency must be stated on the plan of care or in the contract. Keep a written report for each visit with the aide present. Confirm the current (f) text and the MLTC contract.

citations.title: Criminal history record check process
citations.requirement: Request a check for each prospective employee (a). An authorized person signs the DOH form, and the form and two sets of fingerprints go to DOH within 10 business days (excluding weekends and legal holidays) of taking the prints (b). The applicant presents two IDs, one government-issued with signature and at least one with photo (c)(1). Resubmit within 14 days of notice that prints were rejected (c)(3). Temporary approval is allowed pending results, with the §402.4 supervision (d). An expedited review request applies if the person has a prior determination or a pending submission (e).

citations.title: Home Care Worker Registry
citations.requirement: Part 403 applies to every Article 36 licensed agency. The agency must designate at least two individuals to access and enter data in the registry (§403.3(a)), and it must have policies implementing Part 403 (§403.3(b)). Only designated individuals may submit data (§403.3(c)). Within 10 business days after an aide begins providing services, the registry must be updated with employment information including the start date (§403.5(a)(6), as described in DOH DAL 19-21). A person trained in a state-approved program on or after 9/25/2009 may not provide services until posted to the registry (§403.5).

citations.title: Home care services workers (registry)
citations.requirement: Establishes the Home Care Services Worker Registry and the information entered for each worker who completes a state-approved training program (name, address, gender, date of birth, program). Also provides for indicating advanced home health aide status and any limitation or revocation of that status.

citations.title: Licensure of home care services agencies
citations.requirement: A license is required to provide nursing, home health aide or personal care services. PHHPC approval considers public need, character and competence, and financial resources. The application fee is $2,000 (subd. 13), per the fact-checked research.

citations.title: Annual LHCSA registration
citations.requirement: Annual registration since 1/1/2019. Unregistered agencies may not operate or be paid. The late penalty is $500 per month, and missing two registration periods can lead to revocation.

citations.title: Home care worker wage parity
citations.requirement: For Medicaid-funded home care in NYC, Nassau, Suffolk and Westchester: total compensation is the home care aide minimum plus a benefit portion of $2.54/hour (NYC) or $1.67/hour (Nassau, Suffolk, Westchester) from 1/1/2024. Requires an annual certification and an independently audited statement. Records are kept 10 years, per the fact-checked research.

citations.title: Home care aide minimum wage
citations.requirement: Minimum wage for home care aides: $19.65 (NYC, Long Island, Westchester) and $18.65 (rest of state) as of 1/1/2026. This rises to $20.00 and $19.00 on 1/1/2027.

citations.title: Cost reporting
citations.requirement: Cost reports are filed when DOH requires them: within 90 days of notice, with a 30-day correction window (2018 amendments), per the fact-checked research.

citations.title: Application review standards; determinations of public need
citations.requirement: Character, competence and financial feasibility standards, with working capital of at least two months of estimated operating expenses (§765-1.2). Public need rebuttable presumption of no need where 5 or more LHCSAs each actively serve 25+ patients in a county. Initial applicants must commit to serve hard-to-reach groups (§765-1.16(e)). Per the fact-checked research.

citations.cite: DOH MLTC Policy: LHCSA contract limits
citations.title: Licensed Home Care Services Agencies contract guidance
citations.requirement: MLTC plans may contract with no more than 1 LHCSA per 100 enrollees downstate or per 60 rest of state, with at least two LHCSAs per county accepting new enrollees. Exceptions: LHCSAExceptions@health.ny.gov. Per the fact-checked research.

citations.cite: DOH Electronic Visit Verification (21st Century Cures Act, 42 USC 1396b(l))
citations.title: EVV for Medicaid personal care
citations.requirement: EVV is required for Medicaid personal care services from 1/1/2021 (choice model: the agency picks its own vendor), with data sent to the NYS EVV Data Aggregator. It captures date, location, service, people, and start and end times. Per the fact-checked research.

citations.title: Minimum Needs Requirements effective 9/1/2025
citations.requirement: Adults 21+ seeking PCS or CDPAS must need limited assistance with more than two ADLs (more than one ADL with supervision for dementia or Alzheimer's). It applies to initial assessments and reassessments on or after 9/1/2025, and to Medicaid recipients 18+ seeking MLTC or MAP enrollment. Per the fact-checked research.

citations.title: Weekly HERDS reporting by LHCSAs
citations.requirement: Weekly HERDS reporting includes patient census by licensed county. The window opens Tuesday 8:00 a.m. and closes Thursday 2:00 p.m. (since 6/17/2025). Contact hcstatrpts@health.ny.gov. Per the fact-checked research.

citations.cite: NYSDOH LHCSA Policy & Procedure Manual Review Tool (Part B)
citations.title: DOH review tool for LHCSA P&P manuals
citations.requirement: DOH reviewers check P&P manuals against 10 NYCRR 766 (including §766.11(b)-(c)) and Part 403 registry provisions. Use it as the surveyor's checklist.

citations.title: PCA/HHA/AHHA training documentation verification
citations.requirement: When hiring aides, review the available training materials to confirm training from a DOH- or SED-approved program. The materials must include the Home Care Registry aide profile; the training certificate is included if available.

citations.cite: OMIG Audit Protocol: Personal Care Aides (guidance, rev. 5/11/15)
citations.title: Personal care audit criteria
citations.requirement: Audit guidance only; it does not create legal requirements. It describes disallowance of claims where there is no documented RN supervisory visit within 120 days before the sampled date of service. A written report is needed for each visit. The visit frequency should appear on the plan of care or in the contract.

citations.cite: DOH Medicaid Managed Care NYIA guidance
citations.title: MMC guidance on NYIA, plan of care and authorizations
citations.requirement: The plan remains responsible for authorizing services and must record the level, amount, frequency and duration of authorized services in the plan of care, with notice to the enrollee. Plans coordinate with the NYIA on assessments and practitioner orders (18 NYCRR 505.14(b)(2)(iii)).

citations.title: P&P manual and pre-opening survey
citations.requirement: After PHHPC contingent approval, the P&P manual goes to the regional home care office. The regional office must accept it before the pre-opening survey. Per the fact-checked research.

policies.title: Governing Authority, Operator and RN Director of Patient Services Responsibilities
policies.applies_to: Governing authority/operator, administrator, RN Director of Patient Services and all management staff of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To define who is accountable for the operation of [AGENCY NAME] as a New York licensed home care services agency (LHCSA), and to ensure that the agency is directed, staffed and equipped to deliver safe care in compliance with law.
policies.policy: The governing authority (operator) of [AGENCY NAME] is responsible for the operation of the agency and for compliance with all applicable federal, state and local laws (10 NYCRR §766.9(a)-(b)). It adopts and amends the agency's policies (§766.9(d)). It employs at least one licensed, currently registered registered nurse (RN) who is responsible for directing and supervising all patient care (§766.9(h)). It employs or contracts for enough qualified staff to meet patient needs and maintains an adequate office with access to patient records and prompt telephone contact (§766.9(f)-(g)). After contingent approval by the Public Health and Health Planning Council, this manual is submitted to the DOH regional home care office. The agency does not accept patients until the regional office has accepted the manual and the pre-opening survey is complete.

definitions.definition: The person or body legally responsible for the agency, such as the owner, board or members named in the license application. It is referred to in this manual as the operator.
The licensed, currently registered RN employed by the agency to direct and supervise all patient care under 10 NYCRR §766.9(h).
The DOH regional office that reviews and accepts the policy and procedure manual and conducts the pre-opening survey.
The DOH on-site review conducted after the manual is accepted and before the agency may begin to serve patients.

procedures: The governing authority adopts this manual and each later amendment by written resolution, signed and dated by the [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] or other authorized member, and recorded in the governing authority minutes.

After PHHPC contingent approval, the [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] submits the complete manual to the DOH regional home care office. The submission date and any DOH comments are logged in the regulatory correspondence file.

The [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] answers regional office comments in writing, revises the manual and obtains governing authority re-adoption. The agency does not accept any patient or assign any caregiver until the regional office has accepted the manual and the pre-opening survey has been completed.

The governing authority appoints an RN Director of Patient Services before the pre-opening survey. The appointment is documented in writing and the RN's name is kept current in the agency's DOH contact information.

Before appointment and at least annually, the [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] verifies the RN's New York license and current registration through the NYS Education Department online verification. A copy is placed in the personnel file (PER-05).

The agency sets the RN Director's qualifications in the written job description (PER-10). Part 766 does not set a separate administrator credential, so the job description must match the duties actually assigned.

The RN Director directs and supervises all patient care. This includes intake and RN determinations (SVC-02), plans of care (SVC-06), aide supervision (SVC-07), and review of clinical records (REC-01).

If the RN Director position becomes vacant, the governing authority designates a licensed, registered RN in writing within one business day to direct and supervise patient care. It begins recruitment immediately, and no patient care goes unsupervised.

The [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] reviews staffing against the patient census and authorized hours at least monthly, and documents whether staffing is adequate. Staffing shortfalls are reported to the governing authority and recorded in the minutes.
The agency maintains an office at [ADDRESS] with access to patient records and a telephone answered by [PHONE] during published hours. After-hours coverage follows GOV-07.
The governing authority keeps a written emergency plan and orients all employees to it (SAF-05).

The governing authority meets at least quarterly. It reviews the QI committee's written summary (GOV-04), complaint trends (CR-02), incident trends (SAF-02), compliance matters (GOV-05) and the status of regulatory filings (GOV-02, REC-02). Minutes are signed and kept.
The governing authority ensures that the agency's services, service area, charges and payment mechanisms are made public (GOV-02).

The [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] keeps a regulatory calendar of due dates for registration, policy reviews, training, reports and licensure amendments, and reports its status at each governing authority meeting.

responsibilities.duty: Adopts policies; ensures legal compliance; employs an RN Director and sufficient staff; maintains the office; reviews QI and compliance reports; keeps minutes.
Carries out governing authority decisions day to day; submits the manual and regulatory filings; maintains the regulatory calendar; reports to the governing authority.
Directs and supervises all patient care; ensures nursing and clinical policies are followed; reports clinical concerns and quality findings to the governing authority.
Assumes RN Director duties during a documented absence or vacancy.

documentation: Governing authority resolutions and signed minutes (retained at least 3 years)
Manual submission log and DOH correspondence file, including acceptance of the manual and pre-opening survey records
RN Director appointment letter, license verification and job description
Monthly staffing adequacy review
Regulatory calendar

policies.title: Licensure, Counties Served, Annual Registration and Public Information
policies.applies_to: Governing authority, administrator and administrative staff of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To ensure [AGENCY NAME] operates only under a valid LHCSA license, serves only the counties approved on that license, registers every year, and makes required information public.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] provides nursing, home health aide or personal care services only under a license issued under Public Health Law §3605 and approved by the Public Health and Health Planning Council. It serves patients only in the counties named on its license. It registers annually under Public Health Law §3605-b and does not operate or bill while unregistered. It publicly discloses its services, geographic area, charges and payment mechanisms (10 NYCRR §766.9(e)). It keeps its license and required organizational records at its principal New York State office (§766.12(a)(1)). The license is not transferable.

definitions.definition: A licensed home care services agency licensed under Public Health Law Article 36.
The yearly registration required of each LHCSA under Public Health Law §3605-b. Unregistered agencies may not operate or be paid.
A licensing standard under 10 NYCRR §765-1.16. There is a rebuttable presumption of no need in a county where 5 or more LHCSAs each actively serve 25 or more patients.
A DOH-approved change to the license to add a county, service or site.

procedures: The [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] keeps the original license, the PHHPC approval, the organizational documents and the assumed-name certificate (if any) at the principal office at [ADDRESS]. A copy of the license is available to staff and surveyors on request.

The [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] posts a list of the counties authorized on the license in the intake file. Intake staff check every referral address against that list before the referral is accepted (SVC-02).
Intake staff decline referrals for any county not on the license. They refer the person to another licensed agency and log the referral in the intake record.

To add a county, service or site, the [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] contacts the regional home care office or homecareapplications@health.ny.gov, files the administrative amendment, and obtains written approval. The agency does not serve in the new county until approval is received.

Before filing a county amendment, the [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] checks whether the county is subject to the public-need presumption, and documents the evidence (such as the hard-to-reach groups commitment) that the governing authority will rely on.
The [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] keeps the commitment to serve hard-to-reach groups made at application (§765-1.16(e)) in the compliance file. Intake and QI staff review it annually (GOV-04).
The [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] enters the annual registration deadline on the regulatory calendar and starts the registration at least 60 days before the deadline.

The registration is completed, and any fee is paid, before the deadline. The confirmation is filed. If it is late, the governing authority is told immediately. A $500-per-month late penalty applies, and missing two registration periods can lead to revocation.

If registration is not current, the [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] consults the regional office or counsel about whether services may continue. The governing authority records its decision in the minutes. The agency does not bill for any period when it was not registered unless counsel confirms in writing that billing is permitted.

The [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] maintains a public information sheet listing services offered, counties served, charges and accepted payment sources (Medicaid MLTC plans, fee-for-service Medicaid and private pay). It is given to every inquirer and updated within 30 days of any change.
The sheet is reviewed at least annually by the governing authority and whenever rates change (CR-06).
The [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] keeps a current patient roster and a listing of all personnel at the principal office, updated at least monthly.

The agency does not sell, assign or transfer the license. Any change of ownership or control is discussed with counsel before any agreement is signed. A change of ownership requires a new certificate of need application, and no change takes effect before approval (GOV-06).
The agency does not hold itself out as serving any county, or providing any service, that is not on its license in advertising, websites or contracts.

responsibilities.duty: Ensures licensure and registration remain current; approves license amendments and public information; makes decisions on any lapse.
Files amendments and registration; maintains the license file, roster, personnel list and public information sheet.
Verify the county of every referral against the license before acceptance.
Confirms that services accepted fall within the licensed services.

documentation: License, PHHPC approval and organizational documents
Amendment applications and DOH approvals
Annual registration confirmations and receipts
Public information sheet with revision dates
Declined referral log
Current patient roster and personnel list

policies.title: Policy Review and Document Control
policies.applies_to: Governing authority, administrator, RN Director of Patient Services, QI committee and all staff of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To keep every policy and procedure current, approved, accessible and consistent with law, and to ensure staff use only the current version.
policies.policy: Personnel policies are reviewed at least annually (10 NYCRR §766.11(a)). Service policies are reviewed and revised as necessary (§766.2(a)(1)). The written HPN coverage policy is reviewed at least annually (§766.9(o)). The QI committee reviews policies and recommends changes, and the governing authority adopts and amends them (§766.9(d), (l)). The current policy set is kept at the principal office and at every branch office (§766.12(a)(1), (a)(2)).

definitions.definition: This Policy and Procedure Manual, including all adopted amendments, forms and attachments.
The current approved version, held at the principal office and each branch and in the electronic file, with a version number and approval date.
A prior version of a policy, kept in the archive and no longer used by staff.

procedures: Each policy shows a policy ID, title, version number, effective date, last review date and approver. The [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] maintains a master index of all policies.
The [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] holds the only master copy. A paper controlled copy is kept at the principal office at [ADDRESS] and at each branch. An electronic copy is available to all supervisory staff.
The [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] reviews all personnel policies (PER series) at least once every 12 months and records the date and any changes.
The RN Director reviews all service policies (SVC, SAF, CR series) at least annually and whenever a law, DOH or Medicaid guidance, incident or QI finding makes a change necessary.
The HPN coverage policy and 24/7 contact procedure (GOV-07) are reviewed at least once every 12 months, and the review date is written on the policy.
At each quarterly meeting, the QI committee reviews the policies listed on its agenda and records its recommendations in the minutes (GOV-04).
Any staff member may propose a change in writing to the [ADMINISTRATOR NAME]. The proposal is logged and presented to the QI committee at its next meeting, or sooner if there is a safety issue.
The governing authority adopts each revision by signed resolution. The new version becomes effective on the date specified, and the revision is recorded in the revision history.
When a policy changes, the [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] replaces the controlled copies within 5 business days and moves the superseded version to the archive.

The RN Director or [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] trains affected staff on the revision within 30 days of the effective date, or sooner if it affects patient safety. A signed training acknowledgment is placed in each personnel file.

Where a change affects DOH-reviewed content (such as services offered or counties), the [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] confirms with the regional home care office whether notice or an amendment is required before implementing it.
Once a year, the [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] checks that every policy shows a review date within the past 12 months and reports exceptions to the governing authority.
Governing authority and committee minutes are retained at least 3 years. The superseded policy archive is retained at least 3 years from the date of replacement.
Policies are made available for DOH review at any time during survey.

responsibilities.duty: Adopts and amends policies; reviews annual review reports.
Maintains the master index, controlled copies and archive; schedules reviews; keeps training acknowledgments.
Reviews service and clinical policies; drafts revisions; trains staff on changes.
Reviews policies each quarter and recommends changes.
Use only the current version and report policy gaps or conflicts.

documentation: Master policy index and revision history
Annual review log, including personnel policies and HPN coverage policy
Governing authority resolutions and QI committee minutes (3 years)
Training acknowledgments
Archive of superseded versions

policies.title: Quality Improvement Program and QI Committee
policies.applies_to: Governing authority, QI committee members, RN Director of Patient Services, administrator and all staff of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To maintain a continuous quality improvement (QI) program that finds, analyzes and corrects problems in patient care and service delivery, and to ensure that new services are reviewed before they begin.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] operates a continuous quality improvement program, and quality is the responsibility of every staff member at all times (10 NYCRR §766.9(k)). The QI committee includes a consumer and appropriate health professionals and meets at least four times a year (§766.9(l)). At each meeting it reviews policies and reviews clinical records selected at random from current patients and from patients discharged in the past 3 months, plus every case with a patient complaint. It sends a written summary of its findings to the governing authority. Any service the agency has not previously provided in homes goes to the QI committee before routine provision (§766.2(a)(7)).

definitions.definition: The committee of at least one consumer and appropriate health professionals that carries out the review functions of 10 NYCRR §766.9(l).
A member who represents the interests of patients and is not an employee of the agency, as defined by the governing authority in the committee charter.
Records selected by a method that does not allow staff to choose which records are reviewed, such as a random number list.
A written action with a responsible person, a due date and a method for confirming that the action worked.

procedures: The governing authority appoints the QI committee in writing. It includes at least one consumer and appropriate health professionals, including the RN Director of Patient Services. Members and their roles are listed in the committee roster.
The committee meets at least four times a year, at regular intervals. The [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] schedules the dates at the start of the year and records attendance at each meeting.

Before each meeting, the RN Director's designee randomly selects records of current patients and of patients discharged within the past 3 months, using a documented selection method. The sample size is set in the committee charter and recorded in the minutes.
The designee also pulls every complaint case received since the last meeting from the complaint log (CR-02), whether or not the complaint was substantiated.

Committee reviewers use a standard record review tool. It checks the practitioner order, assessment, plan of care, aide supervision visits (SVC-07), documentation of services delivered, incident follow-up, and discharge planning and notice (SVC-12).

At each meeting, the committee reviews the record review findings, complaints, incident and accident trends (SAF-02), missed visit data (SVC-09), and any policies on the agenda (GOV-03). It also reviews infection control and exposure reports (SAF-03, SAF-07).
For each deficiency found, the committee assigns a corrective action plan with a responsible person and due date. The next meeting reviews each open action until it is closed.

Within 30 days of each meeting, the RN Director prepares a written summary of findings, trends and recommendations and sends it to the governing authority. The governing authority acts on it and records its decisions in its minutes.

Before the agency provides any service that it has not previously provided in homes, the RN Director submits a written proposal to the QI committee (SVC-14). The service does not start until the committee has reviewed it and the governing authority has approved it.

Any staff member may report a quality concern to the RN Director at any time, without retaliation. The concern is logged and brought to the next committee meeting, or sooner if there is a safety risk.
Staff are told about QI findings that affect their work, and the RN Director provides training as needed (PER-03).
Committee minutes, record review tools, summaries and corrective action plans are kept for at least 3 years.
The committee reviews the QI program itself once a year, including whether the sampling method, the committee membership and the meeting frequency met this policy.

responsibilities.duty: Appoints the committee, reviews written summaries, acts on findings and approves new services.
Meets at least four times a year; reviews records, complaints and policies; assigns corrective actions.
Prepares the sample, leads reviews, writes the summary and tracks corrective actions.
Schedules meetings, keeps minutes and ensures the governing authority receives the summaries.
Report concerns and take part in corrective actions.

documentation: QI committee roster and charter
Minutes and attendance for each meeting (3 years)
Record sample selection method and review tools
Written summary to the governing authority and the governing authority's response
Corrective action plan log
New service proposals and committee decisions

policies.title: Corporate Compliance, Fraud and Billing Integrity
policies.applies_to: Governing authority, administrator, billing and scheduling staff, RN Director of Patient Services and all employees and contractors of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To prevent, detect and correct fraud, waste and improper billing, and to ensure that [AGENCY NAME] bills Medicaid, MLTC plans and private payers only for authorized services that were actually delivered and documented.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] bills only for services that were ordered, authorized, delivered by a qualified aide and documented. Personal care services must be medically necessary, ordered by a qualified independent practitioner, based on assessment, delivered under a plan of care and supervised by an RN (18 NYCRR §505.14(a)(1)). Personal care orders and services are subject to the OMIG sanctions and overpayment recovery rules in 18 NYCRR Parts 515-518 (§505.14(b)(2)(ii)(i)). The agency keeps patient-care financial records for at least 3 years (10 NYCRR §766.12(a)(3)). Wage parity records are kept for 10 years. The agency adopts a written compliance program and applies it to all employees and contractors. Whether 18 NYCRR Part 521 requires a formal program for the agency's billing volume has not been confirmed, so the governing authority will confirm this with counsel or OMIG and adopt a written program regardless.

definitions.definition: The person designated by the governing authority to run the compliance program. This is [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] unless the governing authority names someone else.
The NYS Office of the Medicaid Inspector General, which audits Medicaid providers and recovers overpayments.
A claim for payment that the agency knows is false, including billing for services not delivered, not authorized or not documented.
A payment received that the agency is not entitled to.
OMIG guidance on how personal care claims are audited. It is guidance and does not itself create legal requirements.

procedures: The governing authority designates a compliance officer in writing. That person reports directly to the governing authority on compliance matters, and the designation is recorded in its minutes.

The compliance officer drafts a written compliance program covering the following: standards of conduct, billing rules, training, a reporting channel, non-retaliation, auditing and corrective action. The governing authority adopts it by resolution. The compliance officer confirms with counsel or OMIG whether Part 521 applies to the agency and records the answer.

All employees and contractors receive compliance training at hire and at least annually (PER-03). The training covers the False Claims Act, the OMIG sanctions rules, accurate timekeeping and how to report concerns. Attendance is documented.

The agency bills a service only when it has a practitioner order, a current authorization from the MLTC plan or social services district (SVC-13), a plan of care, and EVV or timekeeping data showing the aide actually delivered the visit (SVC-10).

Before billing, billing staff compare each claim with the authorization and the aide's visit record. They hold any claim that exceeds authorized hours, falls outside the authorized dates, or has missing or inconsistent time data. They refer exceptions to the RN Director or compliance officer.

Aide time and tasks are documented contemporaneously. Staff do not alter, back-date or create records after the fact without an approved, dated correction entry. Aides are never paid or billed for time when no care was provided.

The RN Director schedules and documents RN supervisory visits (SVC-07), each with a written report. The OMIG audit guidance describes disallowance of claims where no RN supervisory visit is documented within 120 days before the sampled date of service. The agency therefore tracks this and escalates any patient who approaches that limit. The visit frequency is stated in the plan of care.

Staff report any suspected fraud, billing error or improper payment to the compliance officer, or to the governing authority if the concern involves the compliance officer. Reports may be made without giving a name. No one is disciplined or retaliated against for a good-faith report.
The compliance officer investigates reports within 10 business days, keeps a confidential investigation file and presents findings to the governing authority.

If an overpayment is found, the compliance officer works with counsel to quantify it and to report and repay it as the payer or OMIG requires. The governing authority records the corrective action in its minutes.
The compliance officer audits a sample of claims each quarter against orders, authorizations, plans of care, supervisory visits and EVV records. The results are reported to the QI committee (GOV-04).

Before hire and monthly, the compliance officer checks employees and contractors against the OMIG exclusion list and the federal exclusion list. The agency does not employ or bill for the services of an excluded person.
Management or franchise arrangements may not transfer control of billing or of books and records away from the governing authority (GOV-06).
The agency keeps patient-care financial records for at least 3 years, and wage parity records for 10 years. Any longer period required by a payer contract or law applies instead.

The agency cooperates fully with OMIG, DOH and payer audits. The compliance officer coordinates records requests, and no one alters or removes records once an audit or investigation notice is received.

responsibilities.duty: Adopts the compliance program; designates the compliance officer; receives compliance reports; acts on overpayments.
Runs the program; investigates reports; performs audits and exclusion checks; coordinates audits and repayments.
Match claims to orders, authorizations and visit data before billing; hold and refer exceptions.
Ensures supervisory visits and plans of care support billing; reviews clinical documentation concerns.
Document accurately; report concerns; complete compliance training.

documentation: Written compliance program and governing authority resolution
Compliance officer designation
Compliance training attendance records
Compliance report log and investigation files
Quarterly claims audit results
Exclusion screening records
Overpayment calculations and repayment records
Patient-care financial records (3 years) and wage parity records (10 years)

policies.title: Management Contracts, Franchise Agreements and Contracted Services
policies.applies_to: Governing authority, administrator, RN Director of Patient Services and any staff who arrange or oversee contracted personnel or management services at [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To make sure that management contracts, franchise agreements and contracts for patient care services meet New York requirements and do not weaken the governing authority's control or the quality of care.
policies.policy: A management contract or franchise agreement takes effect only with the prior written consent of the Commissioner of Health. [AGENCY NAME] submits the proposal at least 60 days before the proposed effective date (10 NYCRR §766.9(m)(4), (n)(2)). The governing authority keeps control of hiring and firing of the administrator, the books and records, assets and liabilities, and the independent adoption of policies (§766.9(m)(2)(iii), (n)(3)). Services provided by arrangement require a written contract. Contract personnel must meet the personnel requirements of §766.11. The agency remains responsible for the adequacy of contracted services (§766.10(b)-(d)). Nurses or therapists under contract coordinate and integrate their work with the agency's care planning and supervision (§766.10(e)).

definitions.definition: An agreement under which another person or entity manages the agency's operations. It is subject to prior written consent of the Commissioner.
An agreement under which the agency operates under another party's name, system or brand. It is subject to prior written consent of the Commissioner.
Patient care services, such as nursing, therapy or aide services, that the agency provides through an outside person or organization under a written contract.
Individuals who deliver patient care for the agency under a contract rather than as employees.

procedures: No staff member may sign or begin a management contract or franchise agreement. Only the governing authority may approve a proposal, after review by counsel.

The [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] checks that each proposed management or franchise agreement preserves the governing authority's control of hiring and firing the administrator, the books and records, assets and liabilities, and independent adoption of policies, and records the finding.
The [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] submits the proposal to DOH at least 60 days before the proposed effective date. The submission date is logged on the regulatory calendar.
The agreement states that it takes effect only on the Commissioner's written consent. The agency does not allow the manager or franchisor to act under the agreement until consent is in the file.

If a management contract is to be ended for cause, the governing authority sends not more than 60 days' notice, gives written notice to DOH, and prepares a written continuation plan so that patient care and records continue without interruption.

The governing authority reviews every management or franchise agreement at least annually to confirm that control has not shifted and that the terms still comply. Any change to the terms is treated as a new proposal.

Before contracting for patient care services, the RN Director defines the service, the qualifications required and the patients to be served. Services are provided by arrangement only under a written contract signed before work begins.

Each contract states: the services; the personnel qualifications; that §766.11 personnel requirements are met; supervision and coordination with the RN Director; documentation and record access; confidentiality (CR-03); incident and complaint reporting; and the agency's right to end the contract for unsafe or non-compliant care.

Before a contract worker has patient contact, the [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] confirms that the worker meets the same requirements as an employee (PER-01, PER-02, PER-04, PER-03). The agency holds copies or verifies them with the contractor in writing.
Contract nurses and therapists take part in care planning, report to the RN Director and follow the agency's plan of care process (SVC-06, SVC-07). The RN Director reviews their documentation.
The agency remains responsible for contracted services. The QI committee reviews contracted services at least annually, including records, complaints and incidents involving contract staff (GOV-04).

For any contract with a local social services district for personal care, the [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] reviews 10 NYCRR §766.10(f) in full and confirms the requirements with counsel before signing. The agency also confirms the full text of §766.10 with counsel, because only its opening text was reviewed in preparing this manual.
The [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] keeps all patient-care contracts at the principal office (REC-03). Contract files are kept as a record of the governing authority and are available to DOH.

responsibilities.duty: Approves or rejects management, franchise and patient-care contracts; maintains control over the functions it must keep; gives required notices.
Prepares and files proposals; verifies contractor qualifications; keeps contract files; calendars deadlines.
Defines contracted clinical services; supervises and coordinates contract nurses and therapists; reviews the quality of contracted care.
Reviews contracted services each year.
Reviews proposed agreements for consistency with Part 766 and other law.

documentation: Management and franchise proposals, submission dates and Commissioner consent letters
Control checklist for each agreement
Written contracts for all patient-care services
Contractor qualification and personnel verification records
Annual contract review notes and QI committee minutes
Termination notices and continuation plans (if any)

policies.title: Health Provider Network (HPN) Accounts, 24/7 Emergency Contacts and Coverage
policies.applies_to: Governing authority, Operator, RN Director of Patient Services, HPN coordinators, office staff and on-call staff
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] can be reached by the NYS Department of Health (DOH) at any hour, can respond quickly to DOH requests sent through the Health Commerce System's Health Provider Network (HPN), and files its weekly HERDS census report on time.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] maintains active HPN accounts, designates HPN coordinators, and keeps enough trained staff users to respond rapidly to DOH requests, as required by 10 NYCRR §766.9(o). The agency lists 24-hour, seven-day-a-week emergency contacts in the HPN communications directory. It updates the directory whenever personnel roles change and at least monthly. It maintains a written HPN coverage policy consistent with its hours of operation and reviews that policy at least annually. It submits the weekly HERDS patient census, reported by licensed county, within the DOH window of Tuesday 8:00 a.m. to Thursday 2:00 p.m. (DAL DHCBS 25-09).

definitions.definition: The Health Provider Network, the secure DOH web-based system, accessed through the Health Commerce System, through which DOH communicates with licensed providers and collects data.
The agency staff member designated to manage the agency's HPN accounts, assign user roles and keep the communications directory current.
The HPN directory listing the agency's contacts, including the 24/7 emergency contacts DOH uses for urgent notices.
The Health Electronic Response Data System, through which LHCSAs report their weekly patient census by licensed county.
The agency's written policy stating who monitors HPN and responds to DOH communications during and outside business hours.

procedures: The Operator designates a primary HPN coordinator and at least one alternate in writing. The designation is recorded in the HPN coverage policy and in the governing authority minutes.
The HPN coordinator obtains and maintains the agency's HPN account(s) and assigns each user the role needed for the work (directory management, HERDS entry, DOH notices).

The Operator makes sure enough staff hold active HPN user accounts, including at least the coordinator, the alternate and the RN Director of Patient Services, so a DOH request can be answered rapidly even when one person is absent.
The HPN coordinator tests every user's log-in at least quarterly and removes or reassigns accounts the same business day a user leaves the agency or changes roles.

The Operator and RN Director of Patient Services identify the 24/7 emergency contacts. Each contact must be a person with authority to act for the agency and must be reachable by phone at all hours. Names, titles and direct numbers are entered in the HPN communications directory.
The on-call schedule is posted and kept current so that exactly one named emergency contact is responsible for each time period. After-hours calls to [PHONE] forward to the on-call contact.

The HPN coordinator reviews the communications directory on the first business day of every month and updates any name, role or number that has changed. The review date and the coordinator's initials are recorded in the HPN log.

The HPN coordinator updates the directory immediately, and no later than the next business day, whenever a contact's role or phone number changes, a new Operator or RN Director is appointed, or an emergency contact leaves the agency.

The agency maintains a written HPN coverage policy that states who checks HPN, how often, and who responds during business hours, evenings, weekends and holidays. The coverage hours must match the agency's actual hours of operation.

The HPN coordinator and RN Director of Patient Services review the coverage policy at least annually and whenever hours of operation, staffing or the on-call arrangement changes. The Operator approves it and records the review date on the policy (see GOV-03).

The designated user checks HPN for DOH communications at least once each business day. Any DOH request is logged with date and time received, assigned to a responsible person, and answered by the deadline DOH sets; if none is set, the agency's standard is the same business day.

The HPN coordinator submits the weekly HERDS census by licensed county during the DOH window, which opens Tuesday at 8:00 a.m. and closes Thursday at 2:00 p.m. As an agency standard, the entry is completed by Wednesday at 12:00 noon so that Thursday is available for corrections.

The census is compiled from the active patient roster by county of residence. The RN Director of Patient Services or Operator verifies the counts before submission. The coordinator saves the confirmation of submission.

If the agency cannot submit within the window, or HERDS access fails, the HPN coordinator notifies the Operator at once and contacts DOH at hcstatrpts@health.ny.gov to report the problem and to learn how to submit late data. The contact is documented.
The Operator reviews HPN, directory and HERDS compliance quarterly and reports exceptions to the QI Committee (see GOV-04). The governing authority is told of any missed HERDS window.

responsibilities.duty: Adopts this policy, ensures it is reviewed at least annually, and receives reports of any missed DOH deadlines.

policies.title: Patient Rights and Responsibilities
policies.applies_to: All employees, contractors and volunteers providing or supporting patient care; patients and their legally authorized representatives
policies.purpose: To make sure every patient of [AGENCY NAME] knows and can exercise the rights guaranteed under 10 NYCRR §766.1, receives them in writing before care starts, and that the agency can prove it.
policies.policy: The governing authority has adopted written patient rights policies and procedures in accordance with 10 NYCRR §766.1. Each patient receives the statement of rights in writing before care begins, and the agency documents receipt in the clinical record (§766.1(a)(1); §766.6(a)(9)). The patient also receives a statement of the services to be provided and the charges, and is told before care begins how much third-party payers are expected to pay and how much the patient must pay. Every employee providing care must know these rights and promote them (§766.1(b)). When a patient lacks capacity, the legally authorized representative exercises the patient's rights (§766.1(c)). Medicaid and MLTC members also receive the fair hearing and plan appeal notices that apply when their authorization changes.

definitions.definition: An individual receiving home care services from the agency, including a Medicaid personal care recipient or MLTC plan member.
A person with legal authority (for example, a health care agent or court-appointed guardian) to act for a patient who lacks capacity.
The Medicaid administrative hearing available to a recipient who disagrees with a decision to deny, reduce, suspend or stop services.
A review requested by an MLTC plan member of an adverse determination made by the plan.

procedures: The RN Director of Patient Services (or designated RN) gives the written Patient Rights and Responsibilities statement to the patient, or legal representative, at intake and before the first service visit.

The statement lists the rights in §766.1(a): to be told what services will be provided and by whom; to take part in care planning; to refuse care; to complain without reprisal; to be treated with respect and dignity; to privacy of records; and to refuse advanced home health aide tasks. It also states that a patient may complain to the DOH Office of Health Systems Management.

The RN reviews the rights orally with the patient in the patient's preferred language, using an interpreter where needed (see CR-05), and confirms the patient understands. Large print or reading aloud is used for patients with visual or literacy limits.

The patient or representative signs and dates an acknowledgment of receipt. If the patient cannot or will not sign, the RN records the reason and the date and time the information was given orally and in writing.
The signed acknowledgment is placed in the clinical record before the first visit, and the RN notes the date in the intake record (§766.6(a)(9)).

Before care begins, the intake RN or office staff gives the patient a written statement of services and charges and explains the amounts third-party payers are expected to pay and the amount the patient must pay (see CR-06).

If a payer amount or the patient's liability changes, the agency informs the patient orally and in writing within 30 calendar days of the date the agency learns of the change. The notice is documented in the record.

The agency explains the patient's responsibilities: giving accurate health and contact information, treating staff with respect, providing a safe home environment, notifying the agency of schedule cancellations or hospital admissions, and following the plan of care agreed on.

Where a patient lacks capacity, the RN identifies the legally authorized representative, obtains documentation of that authority when it exists, and gives the rights information to that person. The record identifies the representative.

For Medicaid and MLTC patients, the agency gives or confirms receipt of the plan's or district's notice of fair hearing and appeal rights whenever it learns of an authorization reduction, denial, suspension or discontinuation, and tells the patient how to request a fair hearing or plan appeal. Agency staff do not discourage or delay a request.

A patient who refuses a service, or refuses an advanced home health aide task, is not penalized. The RN documents the refusal, explains the risks, and informs the plan of care team and referral source of the change (see SVC-06).
At orientation and annually, each employee providing care is trained on these rights and signs an acknowledgment. The training record is placed in the personnel file (see PER-03).

The RN Director of Patient Services audits a sample of new admission records monthly for the rights acknowledgment, written statement of services and charges, and the pre-care timing. Gaps are corrected immediately and reported to the QI Committee (see GOV-04).
Any patient complaint about rights is handled under CR-02. Suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation is handled under SAF-01.
The governing authority reviews this policy at least annually (see GOV-03).

responsibilities.duty: Adopts and reviews the patient rights policies and ensures all staff are trained.
Ensures rights are given before care, documented in the record, and audited.
Deliver and explain the written rights, services and charges information and obtain the acknowledgment.

policies.title: Patient Complaints and Appeals
policies.applies_to: All employees; governing authority members; patients and their representatives
policies.purpose: To give patients a clear, prompt and reprisal-free process for complaints and appeals as required by 10 NYCRR §766.9(j) and §766.1(a), and to ensure complaints feed the agency's quality improvement program.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] maintains a written complaint procedure. Every complaint is entered in a complaint log with the dates received and resolved. The agency responds in writing to each written complaint, and to each oral complaint when the patient requests it, within 15 days of receipt, explaining findings and decisions to date. The response tells the complainant of the right to appeal. A member or committee of the governing authority reviews each appeal within 30 days of receipt. The patient or designee is told that they may also complain to the DOH Office of Health Systems Management. Complaints include any lack of respect for the patient's property by anyone serving on the agency's behalf. No patient is subject to interference, coercion, discrimination or reprisal for making a complaint. The QI Committee reviews all complaint cases. Complaint records are kept 3 years from resolution.

definitions.definition: Any expression of dissatisfaction by a patient, family member or representative about the care, treatment, staff conduct, respect for property, billing or services of the agency, whether oral or written.
A request by the complainant for governing authority review of the agency's response to the complaint.
The agency's record of each complaint, including the dates received and resolved.
Any adverse action, such as reduced service, threat or discrimination, taken because a patient complained.

procedures: Any employee who receives a complaint, in person, by phone, by email or in writing, records it the same day on the Complaint Intake Form and gives it to the RN Director of Patient Services (or the Operator if the complaint concerns the RN Director) within one business day.
Staff never discourage a complaint. Patients may complain to any employee, to the RN Director of Patient Services, to the Operator at [PHONE], or in writing to [ADDRESS].

The RN Director of Patient Services enters the complaint in the complaint log on the date received, recording complainant, patient, date received, nature of complaint, person assigned, and later the date resolved.

The agency acknowledges receipt promptly, and the assigned reviewer begins an investigation immediately. The reviewer interviews the patient, the aide(s) and the supervisor involved, and reviews the clinical record, schedules and EVV data.

If the complaint alleges abuse, neglect, exploitation, theft or an injury, the reviewer also follows SAF-01 and SAF-02 and notifies the Operator at once. Patient safety actions, such as reassigning the aide, are taken immediately.
Complaints about lack of respect for the patient's property by anyone serving on the agency's behalf are treated as complaints under this policy and investigated the same way.

Within 15 days of receipt, the agency sends the complainant a written response explaining the findings and decisions to date. Oral complaints receive a written response when the patient requests it. If the investigation is not finished, the response states what has been done and what remains.

The written response advises the complainant of the right to appeal and how to do it, and advises the patient or designee that they may complain to the DOH Office of Health Systems Management. The agency inserts the DOH home care complaint hotline number, [DOH HOME CARE COMPLAINT HOTLINE NUMBER], which the Operator verifies against the current DOH listing before each annual manual review.
On receipt of an appeal, the Operator forwards it to a designated member or committee of the governing authority who was not involved in the original response.
The governing authority member or committee reviews the complaint file and issues a written decision to the complainant within 30 days of receipt of the appeal. The decision is recorded in the log.

Medicaid or MLTC members who complain about authorization or hours are also told of their separate plan appeal and fair hearing rights (see CR-01 and SVC-13). The agency notifies the plan of the complaint when it concerns plan-authorized services.
No employee may retaliate against, threaten, discipline or reduce services to a patient or family for complaining. Retaliation by staff is cause for discipline, up to termination.
The RN Director of Patient Services records the resolution date and corrective actions in the log, including retraining or personnel action, and informs the patient of the outcome.
The QI Committee reviews every complaint case at its quarterly meeting, looking for trends and corrective actions, and includes this in its written summary to the governing authority (see GOV-04).
Complaint and grievance records are retained for at least 3 years after resolution and are available to DOH on request (see REC-03).

responsibilities.duty: Reviews appeals within 30 days through a member or committee and receives QI summaries of complaints.
Ensures the procedure is followed, handles complaints involving the RN Director, and verifies the DOH contact information.
Maintains the complaint log, investigates complaints, and issues the 15-day written response.
Accept complaints, record and forward them within one business day, and never retaliate.
Reviews all complaint cases and recommends corrective action.

Complaint Intake Forms and investigation notes
