Before approval, the aide must hold a valid New York driver's license, show proof of the vehicle's registration, inspection and automobile liability insurance, and have an acceptable driving record. The agency should also confirm that its own insurance covers the activity.

If driving is approved, the plan of care must list it. The patient or representative consents in writing, the agency sets a mileage reimbursement rate, and the aide follows seat-belt, no-phone and safe-driving rules. The aide does not transport patients who need medical equipment or lifting beyond the aide's training.

The aide logs the time and mileage for the errand, escort or trip, and the time is recorded through electronic visit verification as part of the visit (SVC-10). Time spent on errands outside the home counts as working time (PER-06).

If an accident, fall or other event occurs during an errand, escort or trip, the aide gets medical help or calls 911 as needed, then calls the on-call RN at [PHONE] and completes an incident report within 24 hours (SAF-02 and SVC-11).

Supervising RNs review errand and escort tasks at each supervisory visit, check that tasks match the plan of care, and look for signs of misuse of money or property (CR-04). Concerns are reported to the RN Director of Patient Services.
The agency tells aides at orientation and annually that errands outside the plan of care, personal use of a patient's vehicle, loans and personal favors are not allowed (PER-07).

responsibilities.duty: Makes sure errands and escort are listed in the plan only if authorized, and approves or denies any exception for driving.
Reviews tasks at visits, verifies receipts and watches for boundary or exploitation concerns.
Performs only authorized errands and escort, handles money as directed and reports incidents.
Sets and enforces the vehicle, insurance, license and mileage standards.

documentation: Authorized plan of care listing errands and escort
Receipt and money-handling log signed by the patient or representative
Written patient consent and Administrator approval if driving is allowed
Aide license, registration and insurance verification, if driving is allowed
Incident reports and supervisory visit notes
Time and mileage records

policies.title: Caregiver Qualifications, Training Credentials and Certification
policies.applies_to: All personal care aides and home health aides, the RN Director of Patient Services, the Administrator and the person responsible for hiring
policies.purpose: To make sure every aide meets New York's qualification and training requirements, and that training is verified before the aide is assigned to a patient.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] employs only aides who meet the qualifications of 10 NYCRR §700.2 (§766.11(b)(1)). For Medicaid personal care, a personal care aide must have completed a DOH-approved home health aide program or the 40-hour personal care aide basic training (18 NYCRR §505.14(e)). The agency's practice is to verify training before the aide is assigned to any patient, and in no case may completion run past the outer limit that the rule allows. Before assigning an aide, the agency reviews the training source and the Home Care Registry aide profile, as directed in DOH guidance DAL DHCBS 20-05. Each position has a written job description stating its education and experience requirements (§766.11(j)). Aides are assigned by licensure, training and demonstrated skills (§766.5(b)(2)).

definitions.definition: An aide who provides personal care and nutritional and environmental support under the supervision of an RN, and who meets the training and qualification requirements of §700.2 and 18 NYCRR §505.14(e).
An aide who has completed a DOH-approved home health aide training program or an approved equivalency examination.
The record of an aide's information in the NYS Home Care Registry, which must be reviewed at hire and is described in PER-09.
The certificate issued by a DOH- or SED-approved program showing the aide completed the required training.

procedures: The Administrator or hiring manager gives each applicant the written job description for the position. It states the required education, experience, training, certification and physical requirements (see PER-10).

At application, the agency asks each aide applicant to bring or provide the training certificate, the name of the training program and the dates of training. The agency does not rely on the applicant's statement alone.

Before hire, the person responsible for hiring reviews the aide's training certificate and any other available training materials to confirm that training came from a DOH- or SED-approved program, as directed in DAL DHCBS 20-05. A copy is placed in the personnel file.

The hiring manager checks the applicant's Home Care Registry aide profile and confirms that it matches the training documentation presented. Discrepancies are resolved before the aide is assigned to a patient.

If the applicant has an HHA certificate, the agency confirms that it comes from a DOH-approved program or the equivalency examination. A PCA who completed a DOH-approved HHA program is not required to repeat the 40-hour PCA training.

If an applicant has not completed approved training, the agency may hire the person as a trainee only if it provides, or refers the applicant to, an approved program. The agency does not assign the person to patient care until training is complete and verified. The Administrator records the plan and the date of completion in the personnel file.

The agency does not use the three-month allowance for completing basic training as a basis for assigning an unqualified aide. Training must be complete, and the certificate on file, before the first patient assignment.
The agency confirms that the aide holds any other credential the job requires, and verifies licenses or certifications in their primary source when the position calls for it.

The RN Director of Patient Services decides on assignments by the aide's training and the patient's needs. For tasks such as transfers, dementia care or special equipment, the RN checks that the aide has documented training and demonstrated skill, or provides training with a return demonstration before assignment (see PER-03 and SVC-07).
The agency enters or confirms the required aide information in the Home Care Registry as described in PER-09, and keeps the aide's registry profile information current.

Medicaid personal care aides must complete in-service training of at least 3 hours every six months, and the agency also meets the Part 766 annual in-service minimum for each aide title (see PER-03). The RN Director of Patient Services tracks in-service hours for each aide.

The Administrator reviews every aide personnel file at hire, at the annual performance evaluation and at least once a year thereafter to confirm that credentials are current. Any aide who lacks required documentation is removed from patient assignments until it is corrected.

If an aide's certification cannot be verified, or documents appear altered or false, the Administrator does not hire or assign the aide, documents the finding and reports to the appropriate authority as required, including the Compliance Officer (GOV-05).

responsibilities.duty: Ensures only qualified aides are hired and assigned, and reviews credential files at least annually.
Matches aide qualifications and demonstrated skills to patient needs and tracks in-service hours.
Reviews training certificates, the Home Care Registry profile and the source of training before the aide is assigned.
Provides complete and truthful training documentation and keeps credentials current.

documentation: Training certificate and program name in the personnel file
Home Care Registry aide profile review, with date and reviewer
Written job description signed by the aide
Skills competency and return demonstration records
In-service hours log
Annual credential review

policies.title: Background Checks, Identity and Reference Verification
policies.applies_to: All prospective and current employees and contracted personnel with direct patient contact, including personal care aides, home health aides, nurses, and supervisors
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] hires only people whose identity, work history, references, and criminal history have been verified as New York requires, so that no one with unverified credentials or an exclusion has unsupervised contact with patients.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] requests a criminal history record check for every prospective employee (10 NYCRR §402.6(a); §766.11(f)). It verifies each person's identity before retention (§766.11(e)). It verifies employment history and references, or recommendations from unrelated persons for those with no prior employment, before the person has patient contact (§766.11(f)). It checks the Home Care Registry profile of each aide and screens all personnel against federal and state exclusion lists. No one provides patient care until every step required by this policy is complete, or until a documented temporary approval is in place with the supervision required under Part 402 (§402.6(d)).

definitions.definition: The fingerprint-based check processed through NYS DOH under 10 NYCRR Part 402 for prospective employees of home care agencies.
The agency staff member designated in writing to sign the DOH criminal history record check form and submit it with fingerprints.
Permission under §402.6(d) to start work pending CHRC results. It is allowed only with the supervision required by §402.4.
The DOH registry maintained under 10 NYCRR Part 403 that holds training and employment information for home care aides.
A list of individuals barred from participating in Medicare or Medicaid, including the HHS-OIG List of Excluded Individuals/Entities (LEIE) and the NYS OMIG exclusion list.

procedures: Before making an offer, the [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] or designee tells each applicant in writing that employment depends on a criminal history record check, identity verification, reference verification, exclusion screening, and Registry verification.
The applicant completes the signed and dated employment application. It must list all employment history, including dates, and a list of references.

The authorized person requests a criminal history record check for the applicant in accordance with §402.6(a). The authorized person is named in writing by the [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] and the name is kept in the compliance file.

The applicant presents two forms of identification in person. One must be government-issued and bear the applicant's signature. At least one must bear the applicant's photograph (§402.6(c)(1)). The authorized person photocopies or scans the IDs and records the date and the reviewer's initials.

The authorized person confirms that the applicant's identity matches the application and the ID presented. This identity verification is completed and documented before the person is retained (§766.11(e)). Any discrepancy is referred to the [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] and the applicant is not retained until it is resolved.

The authorized person signs the DOH criminal history record check form. The form and two sets of fingerprints go to DOH within 10 business days (excluding weekends and legal holidays) of the date the prints were taken (§402.6(b)). The submission date is recorded in the personnel file and on the CHRC tracking log.
If the applicant has a prior determination or a pending submission, the authorized person asks DOH for expedited review as permitted by §402.6(e) and records the request.

If DOH notifies the agency that fingerprints were rejected, the authorized person notifies the applicant the same day and arranges for new prints. The resubmission is made within 14 days of the notice (§402.6(c)(3)). The notice date and resubmission date are logged.

If the agency considers temporary approval pending CHRC results, the [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] and the RN Director of Patient Services first confirm in writing that the §402.4 supervision required under §402.6(d) can be provided. Without that confirmation, the person does not start work. Each temporarily approved person is supervised as §402.4 requires, and the supervision is documented.

Before the person has any patient contact, HR staff verify employment history and contact each reference. For applicants with no prior employment, HR obtains recommendations from persons unrelated to the applicant (§766.11(f)). Each contact is documented with the date, the name and title of the person contacted, what was verified, and the initials of the staff member.
HR staff verify any professional license or certification claimed (such as RN, LPN, HHA, or PCA training certificate) directly with the issuing source and place proof in the personnel file.

Before first assignment, a designated Registry user checks the aide's Home Care Worker Registry profile and confirms the training information. A person trained in a state-approved program on or after 9/25/2009 does not provide services until posted to the Registry (10 NYCRR Part 403, §403.5). See PER-09.

Before hire, and then monthly as agency practice, HR screens every employee and contractor against the HHS-OIG LEIE and the NYS OMIG exclusion list. The date, list searched, and result are recorded. Anyone found on an exclusion list is not hired, or is removed from duty immediately, and the [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] and the compliance officer are notified (see GOV-05).

The [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] reviews the CHRC result when DOH issues it. If the result bars or restricts employment, the person is removed from patient contact immediately and the decision is documented. The agency does not release criminal history results to anyone without a need to know.

HR completes a new-hire verification checklist for each person showing the date each step was completed. The RN Director of Patient Services or HR will not release a first assignment until the checklist is complete and signed.
The compliance officer audits a sample of new-hire files every quarter. Any file missing a verification is corrected immediately and the result is reported to the QI Committee (see GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Designates the authorized person in writing, approves any temporary approval, reviews CHRC results, and ensures no one has patient contact before verification is complete.
Signs and submits the DOH form and fingerprints on time, verifies IDs, tracks rejected prints and resubmissions, and maintains the tracking log.
Verifies employment history, references, and licenses; completes exclusion screening; completes the new-hire checklist.
Check the Registry profile of each aide before first assignment (see PER-09).
Conducts quarterly file audits and reviews exclusion screening results.
Confirms that temporary-approval supervision is provided and does not assign unverified staff to patients.

Copies of the two IDs presented, with date and reviewer initials
Copy of DOH CHRC form, fingerprint submission date, and DOH results

Written designation of the authorized person

policies.title: Orientation, Competency Evaluation and Annual In-Service Training
policies.applies_to: All agency personnel, including personal care aides, home health aides, advanced home health aides (if the agency uses them), nurses, and supervisors
policies.purpose: To make sure every employee is oriented to the agency's policies and procedures, is shown to be competent in the tasks assigned, and receives the annual in-service education that New York requires.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] gives all personnel orientation to agency policies and procedures and ongoing in-service education (10 NYCRR §766.11(i)). Annual in-service is at least 12 hours for home health aides, 6 hours for personal care aides, and 18 hours for advanced home health aides (with medication management, infection control, and injection safety). Aides providing Medicaid personal care also receive 3 hours of in-service each half year, as required by 18 NYCRR §505.14(e). Bloodborne pathogen training is given at hire and every year (§766.11(l)). Where an aide lacks documented training and experience in a task, an RN demonstrates the task and the aide gives a return demonstration at the initial visit (§766.5(d)(1)). No aide is assigned a task until competency is documented.

definitions.definition: Structured training given before or at the start of employment on agency policies, patient rights, the plan of care, infection control, safety, reporting duties, and the employee's job duties.
Continuing education provided after hire, counted in hours and documented by date, topic, trainer, and attendance.
Documented observation of a worker performing a task, with a return demonstration where required, confirming the worker can do it safely.
The aide performs the task while the RN observes and confirms correct technique.
An aide with additional training to perform advanced tasks under RN supervision. This applies only if [AGENCY NAME] employs AHHAs.

procedures: The RN Director of Patient Services (or the designated trainer) holds orientation for each new employee before the employee's first patient assignment. Orientation covers, at minimum: agency policies and procedures; patient rights (see CR-01); the scope of aide duties (see SVC-01); abuse, neglect, and exploitation reporting (see SAF-01); incident reporting (see SAF-02); infection control (see SAF-03); emergency procedures (see SAF-04 and SAF-11 reference SVC-11); privacy (see CR-03); professional boundaries (see PER-07); and electronic visit verification (see SVC-10).
The employee signs an orientation attendance sheet listing the date, topics, hours, and trainer. The sheet is placed in the personnel file.

HR confirms that each aide's qualifying training meets 18 NYCRR §505.14(e): a DOH-approved home health aide program or the 40-hour personal care aide basic training. The training must be completed within 3 months of hire. HR tracks the due date for aides still in training (see PER-01).

Before the aide's first assignment, the RN Director of Patient Services or a delegate RN uses a written task checklist to assess whether the aide has documented training and experience in each task on the client's plan of care.

If the aide lacks documented training and experience in a task, the RN demonstrates the task at the initial service visit and the aide gives a return demonstration, as §766.5(d)(1) provides. This also applies when a change in personnel puts an aide with a client whose tasks the aide has not been trained for. The RN records the date, tasks, and result.

If an aide cannot perform a task safely after instruction, the RN does not assign that task. The RN arranges additional training and a repeat return demonstration. The aide is assigned only tasks for which competency is documented.

The RN gives bloodborne pathogen training at hire, before any occupational exposure, and again every year. The training includes an opportunity for questions to be answered by a person knowledgeable about the subject (29 CFR 1910.1030(g)(2); 10 NYCRR §766.11(l)). See SAF-07.

The RN Director of Patient Services sets an annual in-service calendar. At minimum each aide completes: 6 hours (personal care aide), 12 hours (home health aide), or 18 hours (advanced home health aide, including medication management, infection control, and injection safety) in each year of employment.

For aides providing Medicaid personal care, the calendar schedules at least 3 hours of in-service in each half of the year to meet §505.14(e). The RN Director of Patient Services records in the training file how the semiannual hours count toward the annual total. If the agency is not certain how the hours may be counted, it provides both and does not assume overlap.

In-service topics are selected from: infection control, patient rights, safety and emergency procedures, observation and reporting of changes in condition, dementia and communication, body mechanics and transfers, nutrition and hydration, professional boundaries, and the findings of QI reviews and supervisory visits.

HR keeps an individual training record for each employee showing hours earned, dates, topics, and trainer. HR runs the training tracking report monthly. Anyone more than 60 days behind a due date is reported to the RN Director of Patient Services, who schedules makeup sessions.
Each trainer signs the attendance record. Employees sign for each session. Training hours are credited only for documented attendance.

The RN Director of Patient Services reviews the training program annually with the QI Committee to confirm that content reflects current rules and any problems found through supervision (see GOV-04 and SVC-07).
New services or procedures introduced under SVC-14 are not assigned to staff until the related training is complete and competency is documented.

responsibilities.duty: Designs and approves orientation and in-service content, performs or delegates competency evaluations, and signs off on task readiness.
Demonstrates tasks, observes return demonstrations at initial visits, and documents results.
Maintains training records and the tracking report, and confirms qualifying training and due dates.
Attend orientation and in-service sessions, complete assigned training on time, and perform only tasks for which competency is documented.
Provides time and resources and ensures that no one is assigned to patients before orientation is complete.
